records.text: A blunt Gordok brute who answers the new king with clumsy praise, boasts that he survived by being smart, and warns that another ogre takes the throne if the king leaves. In a fight, he threatens to smash or crush his foe.

A Gordok mage-lord whose combat boasts are as blunt as any brute's: he threatens to smash or crush his foe. His courtly greeting to the new king quickly gives way to awkward flattery and boasts of his own cleverness; he says the Gordok will choose another king if this one leaves.

A Gordok captain with a fighter's blunt manner: he threatens to crush or smash anyone who faces him. His combat routine can include a fear spell, giving his threats a sharper edge than his simple boasts suggest.
A Gordok spirit that speaks in the same blunt combat boasts as the ogres, threatening to crush or smash its foe. Its words sound like a fighter's challenge despite its spectral nature.

A Gordok warlock whose threats are blunt and physical, promising to smash or crush a foe. Outside combat, its routine can summon a Doomguard, hinting at the dangerous demonic magic behind the warlock's plain manner.
A Gordok Reaver is a blunt, aggressive combatant who speaks in short threats about smashing enemies and follows through with a cleaving attack.
A Wildspawn Satyr is a combatant who rallies with a battle shout and becomes enraged when badly wounded.
A Wildspawn Rogue fights with quick, close-quarters strikes, including Sinister Strike.
A Wildspawn Trickster uses paralyzing poison to hinder opponents in combat.
A Wildspawn Betrayer attacks with ranged shots and can knock down opponents who come close.
A Wildspawn Felsworn attacks with Shadow Bolt.
A Wildspawn Shadowstalker is an elite Wildspawn humanoid that can enter stealth. Concealment distinguishes its combat role.
A Wildspawn Hellcaller is an elite Wildspawn humanoid spellcaster. It casts Fireball in combat, giving this role a direct ranged fire attack.
A Petrified Treant is an elite treant that hardens its skin in combat. That defensive ability defines its role in a fight.
An Ironbark Protector is an elite guardian combatant. Its combat move is Trample, a forceful close-range attack that distinguishes it from the other nearby threats.
A Warpwood Guardian is an elite guardian combatant that uses Head Crack. This close-range move distinguishes its fighting role.
A Warpwood Treant is an elite treant that uses Strike.
A Warpwood Tangler is a beast that attacks with lightning and entangling roots.
A Warpwood Stomper is a beast that uses a War Stomp in combat.
A Highborne Summoner of the House of Shen'dralar warns that a demon has escaped and urges others to restrain it. The summoner also fights with fire magic.
Tsu'zee is a named, fleeting presence who vanishes soon after appearing and strikes with a rogue's Sinister Strike.
An Eldreth Seether can become enraged and cast Crimson Fury in combat and Frenzy when badly wounded.
An Eldreth Sorcerer fights with chain lightning.
An Eldreth Apparition is an undead hostile combatant that prepares with Frost Armor and attacks with Frostbolt, Cone of Cold, or Chains of Ice. Its name identifies it with the Eldreth.
An Eldreth Spirit is an undead hostile combatant that uses Banshee Shriek. The name places it among the Eldreth spirits.
An Eldreth Spectre is an undead hostile combatant that can vanish with Greater Invisibility before fighting.
An Eldreth Phantasm is an undead hostile combatant. It attacks with Call of the Graves and can shrink its opponent.
A Skeletal Highborne is an undead hostile combatant that uses Sunder Armor.
A Rotting Highborne is an undead hostile combatant identified by its decayed state.
Arcane Aberration uses Arcane Bolt in combat, giving it a clear arcane attacking role.
Mana Remnant uses Chain Lightning and Blink in combat, combining a lightning attack with short-range repositioning.
Residual Monstrosity uses Arcane Bolt in combat and casts Arcane Blast when targets are within 9 yards.

Prince Tortheldrin is the Shen'dralar ruler, who says he has ruled this kingdom for 10,000 years and is bound to this place. He exchanges stories with visitors, inviting them to share one or hear one; in combat, he challenges those who disrupt the city's sanctity.
Magister Kalendris is a named magister whose combat magic centers on shadow: he uses Shadowform, Mind Blast, Mind Flay, Shadow Word: Pain, Dominate Mind, and Dark Channeling.
Illyanna Ravenoak is an undead combatant in Dire Maul. Her combat actions include Shoot, Multi-Shot, Volley, Concussive Shot, and Immolation Trap, giving her a ranged-and-trap fighting role.

Tendris Warpwood is a treant who treats Dire Maul as his domain, warning that intruders do not belong and calling on the Ancients to rise against them. He is described as holding the Ancient Equine Spirit captive, and his presence is associated with trample and grasping vines.
Zevrim Thornhoof is a demon in Dire Maul who casts Intense Pain in combat.

Old Ironbark is a treant whose words mark release from Zevrim Thornhoof’s control. A related account describes him as helpless and powerless under Zevrim’s control and calls for an end to the torment; he also speaks of needing restoration, without explaining what restoration requires.
Alzzin the Wildshaper holds a corrupt dominion over eastern Dire Maul, with the Felvine lying near him. Bodley's account says Alzzin and his forces ambushed Isalien at the Shrine of Eldretharr.

Immol'thar is a demon imprisoned at the heart of Dire Maul behind a force field powered by pylons. The Shen'dralar Ancient urges adventurers to destroy him as part of ending the city's madness; when provoked, he can go into a frenzy.
King Gordok taunts challengers as "scrubs," insisting that he is king and will stay king forever. In combat he charges opponents and uses Mortal Strike.
A Warpwood Crusher demon that batters opponents with Crush Armor and Trample.
A Whip Lasher demon that strikes opponents from behind with Lash of Pain.
A Gordok Mastiff beast that attacks with Rend.
A Carrion Swarmer beast that attacks with Venom Sting.
A Phase Lasher demon.
A Fel Lash demon whose combat behavior includes Arcane Bolt.
A Wildspawn imp among the local creatures, it reacts when a target comes within range by casting a spell.
A water elemental that has taken residence in Dire Maul's east wing, Hydrospawn is sought for its essence in an arcane study. In combat it uses Riptide and Submersion.
Death Lash carries virulent poison.
The Dire Maul Crystal Totem has a questgiver interaction.

Ironbark the Redeemed, whose strength is waning, offers one service before returning to the Dream: he will open the door to Alzzin when asked. After fulfilling that duty, he says the way is clear and that he is returning whence he came.
A Petrified Guardian in the local area casts Thorns while out of combat.
Ferra is a beast with a combat role, using Maul and charging nearby targets.

Guard Fengus guards the Gordok and recognizes a claimant to the throne as the new king. In that exchange, he offers to make the claimant fierce and crazed. His speech is exuberant and rough; he also fights with a shield charge and bash.

Stomper Kreeg, known as the Drunk, sells Gordok hooch and boasts that it is the best ogre drink. He greets the new boss and offers a look at his stock; he promises the new boss a free sample of better brews. Kreeg speaks in exuberant, rough phrasing.

Guard Slip'kik guards the Gordok. After someone gets past him, he admits he was fooled and vows to watch more closely; in another exchange he offers a magical boost but asks for help breaking the ice. His boasts turn to self-mocking humor, and he fights with a shield charge and bash.
Cho'Rush submits to the new Gordok king and offers to improve the tribute. He points the would-be king toward Mizzle da Crafty for what comes next.

Captain Kromcrush guards the Gordok king and is quick to confront threats. He clashes with Fengus, whom he accuses of calling him a gnoll lover, and tells the king the story of the Gauntlet of Gordok Might: according to Gordok tradition, the elf-prince Tortheldrin stole it from an earlier king. Kromcrush says he can restore the gauntlet's power from its mark.
Guard Mol'dar addresses the new Gordok king with emphatic praise. He says he had heard the king was dead and that they will be hard to kill after this.

Lethtendris is a blood elf mage in Dire Maul who created a web to siphon the area's magical energies. Feralas agents describe her as an outlaw who defied her fellow blood elves; her device is sought because its gathered power could be dangerous.

Knot Thimblejack is a resourceful tailor and leatherworker held in chains in Dire Maul's Gordok wing. He devised an ogre disguise to help someone pass Captain Kromcrush, and suggests repairing a broken trap to catch Guard Slip'kik. He asks for help escaping, then thanks his rescuer and says he will tell his Cartel friends.
Pimgib is tied to Lethtendris's encounter, casting Fireball, Flame Buffet, and Blast Wave.

Pusillin is an imp who taunts pursuers and challenges them to catch him for a key, even feigning friendship when threatened. Azj'Tordin accuses him of stealing his book of incantations and the key to Eldre'Thalas.

The Shen'dralar Ancient of the House of Shen'dralar urges action against the guardians of Immol'thar's prison, Immol'thar, and Prince Tortheldrin, saying the age of immortals has passed and the city's spirits should be laid to rest. It warns strangers to leave before the place consumes them.

Lorekeeper Lydros is an ancient Shen'dralar scholar who says indexing ten thousand years has given him a perspective that makes present troubles seem trivial. He prizes knowledge and history, yet speaks cautiously about the Prince's treatment of Master Winthalus, a high elf in the Prince's domain, and urges discretion around the search for him. Lydros also studies magical texts and offers to turn recovered librams and reagents into arcanums.

Shen'dralar Zealots share a wary, deferential outlook toward their Master and the Lorekeeper. Their remarks warn visitors to respect the Master's meditations and describe a sanctuary few leave. They also voice concern over missing books in Eldre'Thalas, suspecting theft by imps or someone within the estate.
The Shen'dralar Provisioner offers goods from the House of Shen'dralar.

Lorekeeper Javon serves the House of Shen'dralar at the Athenaeum, where he describes books being stolen and recovered repeatedly. He receives returns of several Athenaeum tomes and welcomes more missing books, noting that rewards may change over time.

Lorekeeper Mykos serves the House of Shen'dralar, receiving returns of several class tomes marked by the Athenaeum. He says Kildrath overdramatizes the thefts, citing one tome stolen over 400 times, and explains that the mark prevents unauthorized viewing.

Lorekeeper Kildrath serves the House of Shen'dralar and is distressed that three prized volumes have gone missing: the Codex of Defense, The Arcanist's Cookbook, and Garona: A Study in Stealth and Treachery. He insists the texts must be returned and worries Lydros will be displeased about the Codex.
The Wandering Eye of Kilrogg senses intruders and opens a nether portal; in combat it summons a Netherwalker.
The Eldreth Darter uses Mana Burn in combat and can cast Power Word: Shield on an injured friendly creature.
Arcane Torrent is a creature that uses Forked Lightning and Lightning Cloud in combat.
Arcane Feedback is an elemental that casts Lightning Shield both out of combat and during combat.

The Ancient Equine Spirit is a freed spirit horse of Dire Maul, formerly held by Tendris Warpwood. It is soothed with special horse feed and accepts the offering, then positions itself for the Arcanite Barding to be blessed. The blessing is described as a brief glow before the barding is secured in the rider’s pack.
Revanchion is a demon whose combat repertoire includes Shadow Bolt Volley and Frost Nova.

Falrin Treeshaper, of the Shen'dralar, is an enchanter in Dire Maul's Athenaeum and an old friend of Anthion Harmon. He agrees to enchant Anthion's banner, but first demands ogre warbeads to avenge his brother, killed by ogres. With the requested reagents, he enchants the banner to make Theldren accept a challenge in Blackrock Depths.
